messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning: workload profile & success criteria

Thanks again for the call this morning, Alex — great to hear more about the use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Dedicated for clinical-document summarization and triage across Acme Health's nurse intake workflow.
- Success criteria (proposed): P95 latency <= 200ms for inference path, accuracy/parity on our evaluation prompts within 3% of your current baseline, and sustainable cost target below $0.50 per 1k requests in production profile.

Workload profile you mentioned (please confirm):
- Nominal RPS: 12 requests/sec (steady), expected concurrency: 8 concurrent sessions
- Peak bursts: up to ~120 RPS sustained for ~20-40 seconds during morning batch arrivals
- Average input tokens: 350 tokens per request (patient notes), average output tokens: ~120 tokens
- Typical sequence-length distribution: 60% <512, 30% 512-1024, 10% >1024 tokens

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0: Access & baseline collection (share dataset + access IP allowlist)
- Week 1: Ingest dataset, run smoke tests, calibrate batching & KV cache settings
- Week 2: Load tests reflecting burst patterns, A/B quality checks vs baseline prompts
- Deliverable: performance report + cost projection + recommended config

Ownership:
- Redwood SE: Ben Carter (I will manage infra setup, load tests, and performance tuning)
- Redwood PM: Marissa Cole (success criteria and billing estimates)
- Acme stakeholders: Alex Johnson (product lead) + procurement for contractual items

Attachments: I attached a starter POC metrics template (poc-metrics-template.xlsx) to capture test vectors, success criteria, and measurement plan.

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm the workload numbers above and the success criteria (reply by EOD Tue if possible)
2) Alex/Procurement: if you can send the intake form or PO cadence, we’ll queue the dedicated trial capacity
3) Ben/Marissa: once we have confirmation, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for next Wed to provision trial nodes

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming the numbers below; happy to align on the success criteria with one tweak on cost targets.

Confirmed workload: 
- Nominal RPS: 10-12 RPS (we’ll target 12)
- Concurrency: ~8 worker sessions
- Burst behavior: up to 120 RPS for ~30s during morning triage windows (happens roughly 2x per day)
- Tokens: ~320-380 input tokens (avg 350), outputs ~100-150 tokens

Success criteria: P95 latency <= 200ms is fine. For cost, our internal bar is closer to $0.40 per 1k requests; if you can show a projection within ~$0.40 we’re good.

On procurement: attaching the standard POC intake form and our PO process summary so you have the right contacts and timelines. Procurement — can you confirm whether a short SOW/PO is required for a 30-day trial?

-Alex

Thanks Alex — that all looks good. A couple clarifying items from Redwood's side so we can size the Dedicated trial correctly: 

1) Load test profile: please provide a representative CSV with timestamps (UTC), request counts, and average token lengths (we’ll use this to create replay harness). If you can’t share exact data, a synthetic profile that matches the distribution you quoted will work.
2) Test dataset & evaluation prompts: please share a set of ~200 sample notes and the gold labels you want us to compare against (for parity checks).
3) Access & security: we’ll need an IP allowlist and an expected call volume egress region (we recommend us-west-2 unless you have compliance constraints).

Evaluation acceptance: per Ben’s note, we’ll run a 2-week technical evaluation by default. If you want a strict go/no-go decision, we’ll produce an evaluation report at the end of Week 2 with the KPI measurements.

Proposed kickoff: Wed Jun 2, 2027 at 10:00 AM PT — 30 min to provision and confirm test vectors. Let me know if that works.

Marissa Cole
